title: Finite type algebras have regular prime-local completion maps
statement: Let R be a G-ring and S a finite type R-algebra. For every prime p of S, the completion map S_p -> (S_p)^ is regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PV, proof of Tag 07PV, reduction to polynomial algebras and descent from the complete local case

proof.text: For every maximal ideal of A[X] use the polynomial comparison theorem. Complete its flat local comparison map. The induced map of completions is flat and local, hence faithfully flat; apply regular permanence to descend regularity of the composite to the desired completion map. Apply the maximal-ideal G-ring criterion to obtain polynomial G-ring ascent.

Induct on the number of variables, using the empty-variable equivalence in the base case and the polynomial/finite-successor equivalence in the step. Present the finite type algebra as a quotient of this multivariate polynomial ring by the kernel of a surjective algebra homomorphism. Quotient G-ring permanence and ring-equivalence transport make S a G-ring; its second defining conjunct is exactly the requested conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 07PV, polynomial induction and completion square; formalized by V2
